facts.text: Metairie’s name comes from French métairie, a 12th‑century tenant‑farm term where farmers paid half their harvest to the landowner.
The area that became Metairie was first settled by French colonists in 1719 when Pierre Chartier de Baulne received land near an Acolapissa village on Chapitoulas Road.
Metairie Road, built on an ancient Acolapissa trail, is the oldest road in the New Orleans area and later hosted an electric streetcar in the 1910s.
The East Bank Regional Library, the headquarters of Jefferson Parish’s library system, sits in Metairie and serves the community’s information needs.
Metairie’s high water table led French and Spanish settlers to use above‑ground burial vaults, a practice still seen in historic cemeteries along Metairie Road.
The New Orleans Saints and Pelicans training facilities are located in Metairie, making the suburb a hub for professional football and basketball preparation.
